Definition: probably ultimately from πέλομαι (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell:--sell, whatever is sold.
BiblicalUsage: Poleo means to sell, to barter in the market. Two sparrows are sold for a farthing in Matthew 10:29, and the rich young ruler was told to sell all he had in Matthew 19:21. The money changers sold doves in the temple in John 2:14.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the market has a price for everything except the soul — and the man who sells all for the kingdom finds he bought the only thing that lasts.
